title: Meta-analysis of secure randomised controlled trials of beta-blockade to prevent perioperative death in non-cardiac surgery
authors: Bouri S, Shun-Shin MJ, Cole GD, Mayet J, Francis DP
population: Nine randomised trials of beta-blocker initiation before non-cardiac surgery judged secure, analysed separately from DECREASE I and DECREASE IV; Erasmus Medical Centre investigations found every investigated DECREASE study, DECREASE IV included, insecure, while DECREASE I (1999) lay outside the investigation and was not examined
funder: One author is supported by the British Heart Foundation (FS/10/038).
result: In the nine secure trials, 162 of 5264 patients randomised to beta-blockers and 129 of 5265 randomised to placebo died: relative risk 1.27 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.60), p = 0.04, without heterogeneity (I2 0%). Beta-blockade reduced non-fatal myocardial infarction (relative risk 0.73, p = 0.001) and increased stroke (1.73, p = 0.05) and hypotension (1.51, p < 0.00001); one large trial dominated these results. The two DECREASE trials gave a mortality relative risk of 0.42 (0.15 to 1.23), diverging from the secure trials (p = 0.05). The authors ask guideline bodies to retract recommendations based on these data and estimate that refraining from the European Society of Cardiology recommendation could prevent up to 10,000 deaths a year in the United Kingdom.
